notes.subject: ⟨mi⟩
notes.rationale: Hebrew suffixes on verbs (-נו) rendered as bracketed pronoun 'mi' since Tok Pisin verbs carry no object suffix.

notes.subject: הדיחנו
notes.rationale: 'Cast/thrust me away' (KJV 'cast out') vs JPS 'washed me clean'; chose 'rausim i go ausait' for the thrusting sense.

notes.subject: כתנין
notes.rationale: Could also be 'bikpela pis nogut bilong solwara' (sea-monster); 'traipela snek' keeps the swallowing picture.

translation: Nebukadnetsar, king bilong Bavel, i kaikaiim ⟨mi⟩, i bagarapim ⟨mi⟩ gut; i putim ⟨mi⟩ daun olsem samting i no gat wanpela samting insait; i swarim ⟨mi⟩ olsem traipela snek; i pulimapim bel bilong en wantaim ol gutpela kaikai bilong ⟨mi⟩, na i rausim ⟨mi⟩ i go ausait.

tokens.gloss: i no gat wanpela samting insait
